attrs.evidence: docs/spec/proof-wire/experiment/evidence.mjs -- parseEvidence()/readEvidence()/tryReadEvidence(), imported by run_state.mjs, holdout_runner.mjs and holdout_score_core.mjs, so the run record, every transition receipt, the RESULT, every archived and every live observation document, the challenge set and SPEC-RELEASE.json all cross it. `node evidence.mjs --selftest` states the reader's two claims over 43 vectors: every input it ACCEPTS is read deeply-equal to JSON.parse, so it is STRICTER than JSON and never DIFFERENT from it, and 6 of its refusals are documents JSON.parse accepts. verifyRun() reads the authoritative record itself rather than taking a parsed object from mutable governance/, because a frozen decision function over an untrusted READING is P4.7.1 one argument to the left. Falsifiers AA1 (duplicate status in the run record's bytes), AA2 (in a reachable receipt), AA3 (in the RESULT, refused before its semantics), AA4 (an archived observation naming two implementations, with the RESULT's digest updated to match), AA9 (invalid UTF-8), and AA8 the positive dual: every artifact of an honest PINNED-to-COMPLETE run reads unambiguously and still verifies. Gate `gov-spec` and `gov-nest`; grid boolean evidence-bytes-unambiguous.
attrs.statement: AN AUTHENTICATED EVIDENCE ARTIFACT HAS EXACTLY ONE READING AT THE BYTE BOUNDARY, NOT ONLY AFTER IT HAS BEEN PARSED. P4.7.6 closed the equivocation over PARSED OBJECTS -- collections keyed by identity checked for uniqueness before indexing, every shape closed -- and every reader still began `JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf8"))`, which resolves duplicate object members by keeping the LAST one. By the time a shape check sees a value, the second reading is gone. REPRODUCED against P4.7.6 on the shipped PINNED run by editing raw bytes to `"status":"REVEALED","status":"PINNED"`: a first-occurrence reader sees REVEALED, Node sees PINNED, and BLIND-RUN printed PASS ... PINNED. The same in a reachable transition receipt, in the RESULT, and -- the one that matters for a foreign implementation -- in an archived observation document, where `implementation` is how a measurement is ATTRIBUTED: those bytes re-digest perfectly, because a digest authenticates BYTES and not their READING. So a strict reader belonging to the INSTRUMENT sits ahead of every evidence read: invalid UTF-8, a byte-order mark, a duplicate member name at any depth, an unpaired surrogate (which Node keeps and Go's encoding/json rewrites to U+FFFD, so it would otherwise surface as a spurious interoperability finding), and trailing content are all REFUSED before anything is checked. It PARSES rather than validating-then-parsing, because scanning for duplicates and then handing the bytes to JSON.parse is two implementations of what the bytes mean. It is deliberately NOT the subject's cas.mjs canonical encoder, for the reason run_state.mjs renders its preimage as lines: an instrument may not decide what its evidence says with the encoder belonging to the thing it measures.
